$schema: scenario-inputs v1 — every numeric coefficient used by calculate-study.ts, each traceable to source-manifest.json

local_incremental_power_draw_watts.definition: Incremental GPU/SoC electrical power drawn above idle while the LiteRT GPU delegate is actively generating. MODELED proxy from graphics/synthetic-benchmark power draw, not a direct LLM-inference measurement.

cloud_datacenter_energy_per_1000_output_.definition: Raw GPU compute energy (no PUE) to generate output tokens on server/data-center-class GPU hardware. Central value is the directly-measured Husom et al. regression coefficient. Low value reflects the small-model end of Luccioni et al.'s measured range. High value is this study's own scenario upper bound, informed by (not equal to) the externally-cited BLOOM-176B API figure noted in Luccioni et al., representing a larger, more capable multi-purpose assistant model class.

cloud_prefill_energy_discount_factor.definition: Input (prefill) tokens are charged at this fraction of the per-output-token compute energy rate, reflecting that prefill is typically cheaper per token than autoregressive decode. A simplifying assumption, not independently sourced.

datacenter_pue.definition: Power Usage Effectiveness. Central is the official 2024 industry-wide average. Low reflects publicly reported hyperscale best-in-class sites. High is this study's own conservative bound for older/smaller facilities.

datacenter_onsite_wue_l_per_kwh.definition: On-site direct water consumption per unit of IT (compute) energy, for cooling. Range reflects regional/climate variation reported in Li et al. 2023; central is a large operator's reported annualized average cited in that paper.

grid_ewif_water_l_per_kwh.definition: Off-site electricity-generation water consumption intensity. Central (3.1 L/kWh) is the U.S. national average consumption figure directly reported in Li et al. 2023. Low/high are this study's own scenario band around that single documented point estimate — regional grid water intensity varies substantially; see limitations.md.

network_transmission_energy_kwh_per_gb.definition: Electricity intensity of internet data transmission. Central is the Aslan et al. 2018 revised estimate. Low/high are a 2x scenario band around it. Because chat payloads are kilobytes, not gigabytes, this term is a minor contributor regardless of the exact value — see calculation-notes.md.

client_radio_active_power_watts.source: informed by huang2012_lte_characterization (see calculation-notes.md — not a directly quoted figure)
client_radio_active_power_watts.definition: Phone cellular/WiFi radio active-state power while a cloud request/response is in flight. Order-of-magnitude assumption informed by the LTE radio power-state literature; not independently re-measured for this study.
